info.title: Olauda API
info.description: The API of the Olauda web app.

get.summary:
The group's announcements, newest first, each with whether the member
read it.

post.summary: Remembers the group as where the app opens next time.

get.summary:
Every member may see who else is in the group; only the pseudonyms are
exposed, never emails.

parameters.name: ban
parameters.description: Also keeps the member from joining again.

post.summary: The previous owner stays in the group as an admin.

patch.summary:
The group's profile (name, picture) and configuration (type, Dalton) need
separate permissions.

delete.summary: Tasks of the subject keep its name as a hand-typed one.

get.summary:
The whole timetable without personalization. Readable by every member,
like `/schedule`.

put.summary: Replaces the timetable and the layout of the school day at once.

get.summary: Readable by every member, like `/schedule/subs`.
The group's tasks for the given filters, ordered by due date.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: The archive instead of the current tasks.

parameters.name: personalized
parameters.description: Leaves out tasks of courses the member does not take.

post.summary:
Refused with `DUPLICATE_ITEM` while a task of the same type, subject and
day exists, unless `confirmDuplicate` is set.

get.summary: The timetable as the member sees it.

delete.summary: Clears the member's courses in this group and asks for them again.

patch.summary: Replaces the member's course selection in this group.

get.summary: Liveness check for the deployment.

Sets the cookie whose value every changing request repeats in the
`x-csrf-token` header.

Whether sign-ups are open and the platform is running, for the sign-in
and sign-up pages.
The running announcements the user has yet to read, newest first.

post.summary: Stores the sign-up and mails its confirmation code.

Answers the same whether or not a code was sent, so it reveals nothing
about the address.
Answers the same whether or not the address has an account.

Signs in with email and password. An account with two-factor
authentication gets a pending sign-in instead of a session.

Entering the emailed code with the password chosen at sign-up creates the
account and signs it in.
Trades the emailed code for the token that sets the new password.
Mails the code that lets a passwordless account set its first password.

get.summary:
Tells the sign-in page whether to offer a passkey besides the code. Only
whoever already passed the first factor can ask.
The signed-in user, or `null` without a session.

post.summary: Every other session ends; this one continues with new tokens.
Rotates the session's tokens, which share one cookie across tabs.

patch.summary: Saves the named settings and keeps the others.

get.summary: The tasks the user checked off, in every group.
The tasks the user pinned, in every group.
The tasks the user moved into or kept out of the archive, in every group.

A ZIP of everything stored about the account. It needs a recent sign-in,
as a stolen session must not be enough to take it.

The caller's groups and where the app opens; answers signed-out callers
too, which is how the client learns whether a session exists.
What an invite link leads to; signing in is optional.
The user's private tasks in their order.

post.summary: Adds a private task at the top of the list.

put.summary: Marks a private task as done or open again.

post.summary:
Only a secret from a recent `setup` can be activated, which already
required a recent sign-in.

Shows a new secret, so it needs a recent sign-in: otherwise a stolen
session could tie the account to the thief's authenticator.

get.summary: Sends the browser to Google to sign in.

post.summary:
Finishes a Google sign-up the callback could not complete on its own: the
user has to accept the terms before an account is created.

get.summary:
Where Google sends the browser back; it always redirects into the app,
with the outcome in the query.

post.summary:
A POST rather than a navigation: it needs the CSRF check and lets the
client refresh an expired access token before the flow starts. A linked
Google account is a lasting way in, so it needs a recent sign-in.
Starts a sign-in with any passkey the browser holds for this site.

A new passkey is a lasting way in, so adding one needs a recent sign-in:
otherwise a stolen session could outlive its own revocation. Finishing only
redeems the registration started here.

get.summary:
How the user can confirm who they are, and until when a confirmation
still counts.

post.summary:
A POST rather than a navigation, like linking Google: it needs the CSRF
check and lets the client refresh an expired access token first.

schema.description:
The time windows, ending now, that the server metrics can be shown for. A fixed set keeps
every request to the Hetzner API small and predictable.

get.summary: The security and activity logs, newest or oldest first, a page at a time.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Entries about this account as well as those it caused.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: The part of a type before its first colon, such as `auth`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where the previous page ended; left out for the first page.

schema.description:
How many rows to skip. Anything below zero reads as zero, so a hand-edited
request can never produce a negative offset.
How many rows to return, capped so no request can ask for a whole table.

post.summary: Only superadmins can open a banned group; its invites admit nobody.

schema.description:
How many rows to skip. Anything below zero reads as zero, so a hand-edited
request can never produce a negative offset.
How many rows to return, capped so no request can ask for a whole table.

patch.summary: Picking "owner" hands the group over; the previous owner stays as admin.

post.summary: Ends every session of the user at once.

get.summary: Reports, newest first, each with a snapshot of the reported task.
Running and scheduled announcements, latest start first.

put.summary: Only scheduled announcements can be changed.

post.summary:
Stores a file for a task; it is attached by sending its id along with the
task or to the task's attachments.

A new group's picture is uploaded before the group exists, so this is the
one upload that needs no group membership.

get.summary:
The signed-in user's live updates as server-sent events. The stream ends
when the access token expires, so a revoked session or membership cannot
outlive it; the browser then reconnects with a fresh token.

AccessControls.description:
The switches as stored and as superadmins manage them. Shutdown closes
sign-ups without touching `registration_paused`, so ending it restores
what sign-ups were set to.

AccessStatusDto.description: What the sign-in and sign-up pages need to know before anyone signs in.

AccountSecurityDto.description:
How every account, superadmins included, is secured and signs in. Each
breakdown splits all accounts into disjoint parts that add up to the total.

AccountTopic.description: A part of the recipient's own account.

bannedAt.description: Set while the group is banned.

AdminSystemAnnouncementDto.description:
An announcement as superadmins manage it. Ended ones are never listed:
they are gone for everyone, and the cleanup deletes them.

AnnouncementDto.description: An announcement as one member sees it.

ArchiveCheckedTasks.description:
When checked tasks leave the list for the archive. The task list query
reads the stored names, so they must not change.

createdBy.description:
Recorded by the server; lets the uploader remove their file again from
a task they do not own.

CleanupJobDto.description:
A pg_cron cleanup (or the asset worker), named as scheduled, with the rows
it should already have removed. Anything above zero means it is not running.

CourseSelectionDto.description: A course the user takes, with the subject it belongs to.

CourseSetup.description: Where the caller stands with picking their courses in a group.

CourseType.description: The level of an Abitur course; regular groups have none.

attachmentIds.description: Uploads of the creator to attach, in display order.

confirmDuplicate.description: Creates the task even though one for the same subject and day exists.

oneOf.description: The group type's default when left out.

CreatedDto.description: The answer to creating something, which the client refers to it by.

role.description: `superadmin` or `user`; group roles come with each group.

courses.description: The courses the user takes, in every group.

hasPassword.description: Google-only accounts have no password until they set one.

username.description: The user's pseudonym, the same in every group.

DataArchive.description: The ZIP the export downloads as.

DismissibleNotice.description:
Hints a user can hide for good. Each page keeps its own entry, so hiding a
hint on one page leaves it in place on the others.

EmailActivityDto.description:
The emails Resend sent per day and what became of them, over the same days
as the daily activity.

EmailCode.description:
A code as we mail it: six digits, quick to read off a phone and type on
another device. Anything else is rejected before it can cost a guess.

EmailQuotaDto.description: Emails used in the current billing month of the Resend plan.

limit.description: Absent on plans without a monthly limit.

ErrorBody.description:
The body of every error response. `error` is English and meant for
debugging; clients explain a failure by its `code`.

retryAfter.description: Seconds until a refused action may be tried again.

groupId.description:
The group a ban or mute applies to, so a client with several groups
open knows which one is affected.

oneOf.description: The task a new one would duplicate.

ErrorCode.description: Every reason a client may tell apart and act on.

oneOf.description: Events may have been missed, so everything shown has to be reloaded.

Event.description:
What changed. Events carry no content: a client reloads what shows the
change through the regular endpoints, which authorize every read, so an
event can never reveal more than its recipient may see anyway.

EventLogEntryDto.description:
An entry of either log with the names of the accounts and group it refers
to, as far as they still exist: security events outlive them.

nextCursor.description: Absent once the log is exhausted.

total.description:
How many entries match in all, counted for the first page only, so
scrolling further costs no count of the whole log.

EventSource.description: Which log an entry comes from: the security audit log or the activity log.

FileDto.description: What clients need to display a stored file and build its delivery URLs.

GoogleAuthUrlDto.description: Where the browser goes to continue with Google.

linked.description: Google linked next to a password.

googleOnly.description: No password: the account signs in with Google or a passkey only.

GroupInviteDto.description:
An invite as moderators review it. The token is only handed out while the
invite can still be used.

assignableRoles.description: What the requesting user may change this member's role to.

canRemove.description: Whether the requesting user may remove this member.

muted.description:
Left out unless the requesting user may mute this member: a mute is
between the member and the group's moderators.

canMute.description: Whether the requesting user may mute or unmute this member.

GroupPermissions.description: The lowest role each permission requires.

landingGroupId.description: Where the app opens after sign-in; never used to scope a request.

GroupSummaryDto.description:
A group as the client sees it, including what the caller may do in it, so
the UI never has to re-derive permissions from the raw matrix.

permissions.description: Resolved against the defaults, so clients never need to know them.

banned.description: A superadmin banned the group: only superadmins can still open it.

muted.description: The caller may read the group but not change anything in it.

GroupType.description:
How a group organises its subjects and its schedule.

A regular group is one class that attends every lesson together. An Abitur
group is a whole year in which nearly every lesson belongs to a single
course, so lessons are scheduled per course instead of per subject.

alreadyMember.description: The user was a member before; the invite stays unused.

token.description: The secret the invite link carries.

InvitePreviewDto.description:
What an invite link shows before joining. The group's id is only revealed
to members, so the preview stays anonymous for everyone else.

subjectId.description: `None` when the subject was typed in by hand instead of picked.

subjectName.description: A `common.subjects.*` key or the name the group owner typed.

takesCourse.description: Whether the member takes the task's course.

createdBy.description: `None` once the creator deleted their account.

createdByName.description: The creator's pseudonym, the same in every group.

createdByEmail.description: Only for superadmins, who need it to follow up on reports.

hiddenByCourses.description:
How many tasks a personalized list left out because they belong to
courses the member does not take.

ItemSubjectDto.description:
What a task is about: a subject of the group, optionally narrowed to one of
its courses, or a subject typed in by hand that the group does not offer.

LessonDto.description: A lesson of the weekly timetable.

duration.description: How many slots the lesson spans.

courseId.description: Set when the lesson belongs to one course of its subject only.

email.description: The address the provider account belongs to.

ids.description: Clearing all sends every unread id at once.

MemberRole.description:
A member's role as clients see it. Ownership lives in `groups.owner_id`
rather than `user_roles`, so it is folded in here to keep the single-owner
invariant enforced by the schema instead of by a second role row.

MetricPoint.description:
One sample of a time series: when it was taken, in Unix seconds, and its
value, which is `null` where Hetzner has no number and charts show a gap.

MfaChallengeDto.description: What the second-factor step of a sign-in may offer.

expiresIn.description: Seconds left to finish the sign-in.

MfaSetupDto.description: A new authenticator secret, valid until confirmed with a code from it.

secret.description: Base32, for typing into an authenticator app by hand.

recoveryCodesLeft.description: Set when a recovery code was used, so the client can warn early.
Only while two-factor authentication is on.

MoveTodoDto.description: Moves a private task right below another, or to the top without one.

PasskeyChallengeDto.description:
A started passkey check: the options for the browser and the id to finish
it with.

userHandle.description: The user handle the passkeys carry, base64url-encoded.

credentialId.description:
Base64url, as the browser reports it, so the client can tell the
passkey manager which credentials still exist.

oneOf.description: Required when the account has two-factor authentication on.

PreferencesDto.description:
The settings as stored. Settings the user never changed are absent, and
the client applies its defaults for them.

recentUntil.description: Until when the last confirmation still counts; `None` once it lapsed.

RecoveryCodesDto.description: Shown this once; only their hashes are stored.

contentDeleted.description: The reported task no longer exists; only its snapshot is left.

ReportedTaskDto.description:
The reported task as it was when reported, so the report still shows it
after the task is gone. Snapshots taken by earlier versions lack some
fields, which is why most of them may be missing.

resetToken.description: Sent along with the new password.

ResourceType.description:
Cloudinary keeps images, which it can transform on delivery, apart from raw
files, which it serves as they are.

SaveSystemAnnouncementDto.description: The body for both posting and rescheduling an announcement.

endsAt.description: Omitted to show the announcement until it is deleted.

ScheduleConfigDto.description: When the school day starts and how its slots and breaks are laid out.

breaks.description: Minutes of break after a slot, on every day without breaks of its own.

dayBreaks.description: The days whose breaks differ, each with all of its breaks.

hiddenByCourses.description:
How many lessons a personalized timetable left out because they belong
to courses the member does not take.

id.description: Left out for a new lesson.

ScheduleSubDto.description:
The one change a lesson carries in one week, replacing whatever change it
had that week before.

SecondFactorBreakdown.description: Authenticator app (TOTP) and passkeys, each on its own or both.

SecondFactorProof.description:
What the user offers as their second factor, sent as `{ "code": "…" }` or
`{ "recoveryCode": "…" }`.

ServerMetricsDto.description:
The window is sent along so charts span all of it, even where the series
start late or have gaps.

currentFamilyId.description: The session the request was made in.

twoFactor.description: Not a way to sign in, but what each of them asks for in addition.

requiresMfa.description: The password was right; the second factor is asked next.

pendingSignUps.description: Sign-ups whose link has not been opened yet; they are no accounts.

SubjectCategory.description:
How members pick a subject's courses. Both sets describe how a member picks
a course, never how a course is graded.

name.description: A `common.subjects.*` key or the name the group owner typed.

SubstitutionDto.description: A change to one week: a lesson cancelled, moved or added.

SystemAnnouncementDto.description: A running announcement a user has yet to read.

Theme.description: The colour scheme a user picked; `System` follows the device.

TimeColor.description: How close a task is to its due date.

TodoContentDto.description: Creates a private task or replaces the text of an existing one.

TodoDto.description: A private task, decrypted for its owner.

position.description: A fractional index; the list is sorted by it.

UpdateAccessControlsDto.description:
Each switch is changed only when sent, so two admins flipping different
switches at once never undo each other. Serialized as is for the audit log.

UpdateCourseDto.description: A course keeps its type when none is sent.

UpdateEditorNoteDto.description: An empty note removes the current one.

UpdateGroupPermissionsDto.description: Only the permissions to change; the others keep their current role.

avatarId.description: An upload from `/uploads/group-avatar`; `null` removes the picture.

UpdatePreferencesDto.description:
The settings a request changes; omitted ones keep their stored value. Every
field has a closed type, so the stored preferences stay small and readable
by whatever reads them.

UploadDto.description:
A file uploaded for a task that is not attached yet. Its `id` is what the
uploader sends to attach it.

UploadForm.description: The multipart form every upload sends: the file in a field named `file`.

muted.description: Promoting a muted member lifts the mute.

VisibilityStatus.description:
Where a member moved a task against its natural place: into the archive,
or kept in the list although it would have been archived.

WeekStart.description:
A school week, named by its Monday. Any other day is rejected while
deserializing, so a week can only ever be named one way.

WeeklyRhythmDto.description:
When in the week the app is used, in German local time. Each cell counts a
user at most once per day, so one person reloading the app all evening
does not outweigh a class opening it once.

weeks.description: Whole weeks the counts span, so every hour of the week is sampled equally often.

activeUsers.description: Rows run Monday to Sunday, columns from 0:00 to 23:00.

Window_AdminGroupDto.description:
The rows of a list from an offset on, with how many match in all, so the
client can size its scrollbar before it has loaded everything.

bannedAt.description: Set while the group is banned.

Window_AdminUserDto.description:
The rows of a list from an offset on, with how many match in all, so the
client can size its scrollbar before it has loaded everything.
